Fields are the LAST cycle number a given audit type was run, or null if never done / not yet backfilled. Update this file in the SAME cycle you run any of these audit types on an Actor -- add/replace the relevant field with the current cycle number and a one-line note. Keys: varied_test (plain filter-combo rotation), enum_audit (checked enum/vocabulary fields for structurally-dead values), unreachable_remedy (checked that a zero-row message's suggested fix is actually reachable), competitor_audit (compared price/features against the named competitor). Dates below are backfilled from cycles 797-814's own summaries (already read this session, not fresh archaeology) -- treat gaps (nulls) as real unknowns, not omissions. app-store-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 833: only one real schema enum, `sort` (mostRecent/mostHelpful/favorable/critical). Unlike every other Actor in the facet-diff rotation, Apple's iTunes RSS review feed (itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/customerreviews/id=<id>/sortBy=<X>/page=<N>/json) is directly reachable from this box (no proxy needed, unlike google-news-scraper) -- probed sortBy directly with 13 candidate values incl. the 2 real ones plus 11 plausible-but-unlisted guesses (mostFavorable, mostCritical, topRated, newest, oldest, recent, helpful, rating, relevance, popular, trending). Only mostRecent/mostHelpful (the code's actual 2 API values) returned real entries (50 each); every other candidate returned HTTP 200 with an empty feed (no `entry` key at all) or HTTP 500 -- confirmed by inspecting the raw JSON body, not just entry count. favorable/critical are already correctly documented as client-side re-sorts of mostRecent, not real API params, so the 4-value schema enum is exhaustive and accurate. Clean audit, no code change. NOTE: cycle 832's queue note calling this 'the last enum_audit: null Actor' was wrong -- a fresh count after this cycle shows 12 Actors still null (ats-jobs, eu-ted-tenders, google-play-reviews, nih-reporter, remote-jobs, sam-gov-opportunities, sec-insider-trades, shopify-products, steam-reviews, substack, trademark-search, uk-find-a-tender). The rotation is not done; see queue.md. cycle 845: cycle 843/844 generalization applied here (watch baseline diffed against its own row shape). Apple keeps a review id stable when its author edits their own star rating (feed comment verified live 2026-09-26: a raw RSS entry has only author/rating/title/content/version/votes -- no developer-response field at all, unlike Google Play, so scoreChanged is the only applicable event here, not developerReplied/replyRemoved). Watch baseline was seenIds only -- no rating snapshot -- so an edited review was silently indistinguishable from an unedited one forever. Shipped watchEvents ([new, scoreChanged], empty = both) + watchEvent/previousScore output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (rating 1-5, 0 = pre-845 unknown, never fires) parallel to seenIds. Verified via 5 local round-trip scenarios against real live Apple review data (patching the LOCAL watch KV record, same technique as production KV patches in cycles 843/844, just local so nothing needed cleanup): (1) patched baseline rating differs from live rating + scoreChanged in watchEvents -> fires correctly with correct previousScore, exactly 1 of 20 pushed; (2) same patch + watchEvents:[new] (scoreChanged excluded) -> correctly silent, watchEventsFiltered counted, meta still updated to the live value so it cannot re-fire later; (3) meta silently re-synced after a fire -> third run byte-idempotent (0 pushed); (4) seenMeta key deleted entirely (pre-845 record simulation) -> zero false events, correct predates-change-detection log line; (5) a genuinely-absent id -> delivered as watchEvent:new, previousScore:null. Non-watch default-input regression byte-identical locally AND live on the platform (build 0.1.63, 5/5 charged). check-fail-ordering allowlist line numbers re-verified and updated (907/1146/1162, shifted from 815/1054/1070 by this change -- same 3 guard conditions read live in source, still safe). check-registry-fields/check-code-fields/check-readme-samples all clean after adding watchEvent/previousScore to registry.json output_fields + dataset_schema.json + README (input table, Watch mode section, Use cases bullet, new FAQ entry).
app-store-reviews-scraper.varied_test_note: cycle 1089: GROWTH slot, fleet-oldest varied_test (1037). FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BILLABLE BUG, not just a clean negative. Combo: multi-country array with an explicit country PLUS a second country whose countryFallback probe lands on that same explicit country -- countries:["bt","us"] + countryFallback:true (Bhutan, id bt, genuinely has 0 reviews for Notion id1232780281, verified free via direct itunes.apple.com RSS probe before spending anything; its fallback probe order PROBE_COUNTRIES=[us,gb,ca,au,de] hits 'us' first, which the SAME run already also scrapes directly). Root cause: `seen` (per-reviewId dedup Set) was created fresh inside scrapeAppCountry() per (appId,country) pair, so nothing prevented the identical review (same reviewId) from being pushed and CHARGED twice -- once under the bt/fallback pair, once under the direct us pair -- live-reproduced pre-fix: 16 rows requested, 8 unique reviewIds each appearing exactly twice, byte-identical content both times. Not disclosed anywhere in the README. Fix (build 0.1.70, source 0.1.10->0.1.11): hoisted a `crossCountrySeen` Set to once-per-appId scope (outer apps-loop, before the countries loop) and threaded it into both scrapeAppCountry() call sites (direct + the countryFallback retry) instead of each call creating its own; reviewId namespace is globally unique per Apple review so cross-country dedup can never conflate two genuinely different reviews. Verified live post-fix on the exact repro input: 14/14 unique reviewIds, 0 duplicates, bt-fallback rows correctly tagged (requestedCountry:bt, fallbackUsed:true) then us-direct rows correctly continue with NEW reviews beyond what bt's fallback already delivered (no re-fetch-and-skip waste). Negative-control regression: default test_input.json (single country, no fallback triggered) unchanged, 10/10 unique. README FAQ entry added (v0.1.11) disclosing the fix. Build 0.1.71 (README) verified live via the build's readme field. All standing checks clean after (check-pricing 24/29/0, check-charges 24/24, check-competitor-claims 62/0 + 40/0).

README 'podcasts' output section documents the keep-first-term behavior. package 0.1.4->0.1.5, builds 0.1.52 (code) + 0.1.53 (README) pushed. | cycle 986: varied_test combo never exercised before -- dataType 'episodes' on the PLAIN Apple lookup API path (useRssForFullArchive off, the default) with minReleaseDate/maxReleaseDate set to a window outside Apple's most-recent-episode cap. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL DISCLOSURE BUG: episodePassesFilters() correctly excludes every episode outside the date window (that part was already right, and the RSS 'wholeFeed' path already had its own warning for the equivalent case since an earlier cycle), but the plain Apple-lookup-API path had NO warning at all when this happened, and pushEpisodeRows()'s return value (`got`, the count WALKED) stayed nonzero even though `kept` was 0 -- so the run fell through every emptyIds/failedIds/depthCapped branch in the final status-message logic and landed on the generic fallback: 'No results -- no valid podcast IDs could be parsed from your input.' Live-reproduced on id1434243584 (Lex Fridman, 500+ episodes) with minReleaseDate/maxReleaseDate=2019-01: log showed '100 episodes fetched, 0 kept after filters' yet the buyer-facing status message flatly denied a valid podcast ID was ever parsed -- actively wrong, not just silent, for a namable and common case (any date/duration/explicit filter set outside Apple's ~200-most-recent-episode window on the non-RSS path). Fixed (build 0.1.51): scrapeEpisodes() now also returns whether it used the RSS wholeFeed path; the per-id loop detects got>0 && kept===0 && !wholeFeed && filters-set and records the id in a new `windowFilteredIds` list with its own log.warning naming the cap and pointing at useRssForFullArchive; wired into both the pushed===0 'why' chain (ahead of the generic fallback) and a new pushed>0 branch (parallel to depthCapped) for the partial-fleet case. Live-verified 2 ways post-push: (1) same repro input -> statusMessage now correctly reads 'Apple's lookup API only returned each show's recent episode window for: 1434243584, and your minReleaseDate (2019-01-01) / maxReleaseDate (2019-01-31) filter(s) removed all of them -- turn on \"useRssForFullArchive\" to search the full archive instead.'; (2) default-input regression gate SUCCEEDED, chargedEventCounts {result: 46}, statusMessage None (unaffected). check-fail-ordering flagged the known-safe h289 seed gate at its shifted line (1069->1096, ~27 net lines added above it by this fix) -- re-verified the guard condition is byte-identical, allowlist updated, back to 0 suspects. check-pricing 0 drift/29, check-charges 24/24, check-code-fields/check-registry-fields/check-readme-samples all 0 drift, 3 services active, /health + /tools/apple-podcasts-scraper both 200. | cycle 893: FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG affecting a fleet-wide pattern, not just this Actor. input_schema.json podcasts field carried BOTH default and prefill = the Lex Fridman Podcast URL. Apify merges an input_schema default into ANY run (API/CLI/scheduler) that omits the field entirely -- so a buyer calling with only searchTerms set (the documented "find shows by keyword instead of ... giving URLs" path) silently ALSO got Lex Fridman Podcast episodes mixed into results with no warning, sharing the maxResults budget and starving the actual request (live-verified: searchTerms:["Darknet Diaries"], maxResults=6 returned 3 Lex Fridman rows + 3 real Darknet Diaries rows before the fix). Root cause: Apify distinguishes prefill (UI-only, never sent on omission) from default (merged into every run missing the field, including API calls) -- confirmed via Apify docs. Fix: removed the default key from podcasts in .actor/input_schema.json, kept prefill (Console one-click run UX unaffected). Live-verified post-push (build 0.1.48): searchTerms-only run now returns 6/6 genuine Darknet Diaries rows, 0 Lex Fridman; explicit podcasts input unchanged/still works; fully-empty input now fails cleanly via the Actor's own "provide at least one" validation instead of silently running Lex Fridman. Same default/prefill shape found and fixed in the SAME cycle on google-news-scraper (queries) and steam-reviews-scraper (apps) -- see their own varied_test notes. Not yet checked: app-store-reviews-scraper (apps/appNames) and google-play-reviews-scraper (appIds/searchTerms) have the same field shape and were NOT tested this cycle -- flagged in queue.md for the next QUALITY slot. | cycle 935: varied_test combo never exercised before -- watchLabel (episodes watch mode) crossed with MULTIPLE raw-RSS-only podcasts (no Apple id) in the same podcasts[] input. Found and FIXED a real cross-show identity collision: pushEpisodeRows() built watchId as `${row.collectionId ?? 'feed'}:${episodeId||episodeGuid||title}` -- every RSS-only show (collectionId always null for them, since scrapeEpisodesFromFeed passes null) fell back to the SAME literal string 'feed', not a per-show key, even though the adjacent floorKey/pairFloors logic already correctly disambiguates shows via `feed:${feedUrl}`. Reproduced live end-to-end with two synthetic local RSS feeds sharing an episode guid ("ep1", a realistic collision for cheap/DIY feed generators that guid by sequential per-show number): baseline over both feeds recorded only 1 seenIds entry instead of 2, and a later genuinely-new episode published on the second show (own distinct title/date, but happened to reuse guid "ep1") was silently reported as already-delivered -- 0 pushed, 0 charged, no warning, permanently invisible under that watch label. Fixed by falling back to the already-unique `floorKey` (not the literal 'feed') in the watchId formula -- zero behavior change for the Apple-ID path, where collectionId is always set and the fallback never triggers. Verified 3 ways + live: (1) local baseline with the fix now correctly records 2 distinct seenIds (`feed:<url1>:ep1`, `feed:<url2>:ep1`); (2) the same later-new-episode scenario is now correctly delivered (1 pushed) once its guid is genuinely its own; (3) Apple-ID watch regression byte-identical (5/5 seenIds unchanged, same `<collectionId>:<episodeId>` shape). Live on the platform (build 0.1.50): default-input gate SUCCEEDED 5/5 charged; a real single-feed raw-RSS watch baseline (feeds.simplecast.com) persisted seenIds as `feed:<feedUrl>:<guid>` in the shared production KV store, confirmed via the API, then the test record was deleted.
apple-podcasts-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 853: CLEAN NEGATIVE, formally recorded. Cycle 852 guessed this Actor would be the fleet's next counter-field case (rating/review counts, like hacker-news-scraper) -- wrong guess, because watchLabel is explicitly restricted to dataType="episodes" only (src/main.js:103-112); review counts/ratings live under dataType="reviews"/"podcasts", which have no watch mode at all, so the counter-mutation risk never reaches watch-mode code. Checked the episodes watch path itself instead: baseline is a bare id Set (watchId = collectionId:episodeId|episodeGuid|title, main.js:610), no snapshot of any field. But the README (line 40, "Watch mode" section) promises ONLY new-episode detection ("only episodes not delivered under that label before") -- unlike every other watch-mode Actor in the fleet (Shopify/Play/App Store/Steam/ATS/court-records/HN), it never promises a field-change alert on an already-delivered id, so the watch-subset-shape defect (a promised field-change silently missed because the baseline is narrower than the row) cannot apply here by definition -- there is no promised change signal to miss. Checked the plausible mutation candidates anyway (explicit-tag correction, duration correction, releaseDate correction under a stable episodeId) and confirmed episodePassesFilters() runs BEFORE the watchSeen check (main.js:607-616), so an episode that initially fails a filter (e.g. explicitFilter=clean excluding a mistagged-explicit episode) is never added to the baseline and self-heals if corrected later -- same accidental-coverage shape Play had (cycle 844). No code change.

Closed queue item 0-TODO-h855-pagination. ROOT CAUSE, reproduced live before touching code: Postgres sorts NULLs FIRST on a DESC sort, and schedule_a/schedule_b were queried with sort=-contribution_receipt_date / -disbursement_date and NO sort_nulls_last (schedule_e has always had sort_nulls_last:'true' -- A and B were the odd ones out). A real minority of Schedule A/B rows have a NULL date (F3X filers leave the itemization date blank), so any match set containing one starts with a block of dateless rows, and inside that block FEC's keyset cursor is {last_index, sort_null_only:true} with NO last_<date> value. The code explicitly stripped sort_null_only from the cursor ('a flag, not a cursor value'), so page 2 carried last_index alone -> HTTP 422 'both values from the previous page's last_indexes object are needed'. Verified: unfiltered 2026 schedule_a page 1 = 100 rows, ALL dates null, li={last_index, sort_null_only:true}; replaying page 2 with last_index only = 422 (the exact cycle-855 error), with sort_null_only=true = 200. KEY FINDING -- forwarding sort_null_only ALONE IS NOT A FIX, it converts a loud failure into SILENT TRUNCATION: on a deliberately mixed 2-committee match set (C00406892 = 320 dateless rows, C00002469 = 13,693 dated rows) the sort_null_only walk delivered all 320 dateless rows then returned last_indexes={} at page 5 -- i.e. 'exhausted' -- never reaching ANY of the 13,693 dated rows. A PPE buyer would be charged for 320 useless rows and told that was the whole result set. FIX = both halves: (1) primary -- sort_nulls_last:'true' added to schedule_a and schedule_b (parity with schedule_e), so dateless rows go to the TAIL and the useful walk always carries a real date cursor; (2) defensive -- stop stripping sort_null_only (normalised to the string 'true', false/null dropped) so the trailing null block pages instead of 422ing. VERIFIED on platform build 0.1.31: same mixed-set walk with sort_nulls_last started at the newest dated rows and paged 8+ pages on a proper date cursor; a real filtered run (donorEmployer BOEING, electionYear 2026, maxResults 45) SUCCEEDED across 3 pages -- 45 rows, 0 nulls, dates verified strictly descending 2026-08-31 -> 2026-08-27, so the page-2/3 cursors genuinely work; default-input gate (candidateName Warren) SUCCEEDED, 3 results, no regression. All 8 standing checks clean, 0 drift. NEW BEHAVIOUR / NOT A REGRESSION BUT WORTH KNOWING: sort_nulls_last makes the fully UNFILTERED contributions scan (electionYear only, ~173M matching rows) too expensive upstream -- it 504s on curl and now times out fecGet's 30s request budget on page 1, so that one shape fails with 0 rows charged instead of failing with 100 dateless rows charged. Judged net-positive and shipped; the unactionable timeout message is queued as 0-TODO-h856-unfiltered. The trailing-null-block transition (half 2) is defensive and NOT live-verified -- reaching it needs all dated rows exhausted first (137+ pages on the smallest mixed set found), so it was out of budget to prove.

grants-gov-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 860: the watch-subset-shape sweep's FIRST real defect (the previous 6 Actors were clean negatives). The tracked field SET is complete (closeDate/docType/oppStatus/awardCeiling/awardFloor/lastUpdatedDate + md5 eligHash -- a genuine subset of what Grants.gov can mutate). The defect is one level up: change detection lives INSIDE the per-row walk (main.js onBatch), so it can only ever compare an opportunity that is still in this run's match set -- which makes a FILTER ON A FIELD watchChanges TRACKS self-defeating: the very mutation the buyer is watching for is what removes the row from view. This bit the DEFAULT input: oppStatuses defaults to ['forecasted','posted'], so the headline advertised event (posted -> closed/archived) was silently unreachable unless the buyer widened oppStatuses by hand. Proven live against the real API BEFORE coding (2026-09-26, keyword 'wildfire'): default statuses = 21 hits, ZERO closed; oppStatuses=closed = 380 fully disjoint hits including ids 363103 (closed 09/17/2026) and 363336 (closed 08/28/2026) -- rows a month-old baseline would be holding, whose closure could never be reported. Same trap on closeDateFrom/To + closesWithinDays (deadline moves out of the window), minAwardAmount/maxAwardAmount (ceiling leaves the range) and eligibilities. NOT fixable by widening the walk ourselves: `archived` is hundreds of thousands of rows and enriching them would blow the time budget while delivering opportunities the buyer never asked for. Shipped instead (build 0.1.37 / source 0.1.6): a computed watchChangeBlindFilters list, 2 loud log warnings (split into 2 lines BECAUSE build 0.1.36's single combined line was truncated live by the platform with '[line-too-long]', cutting off exactly the half that says what to do), RUN_SUMMARY.watchChangeBlindFilters (null outside watch mode, [] when nothing is blinding), a README FAQ entry with the live numbers, and a corrected watchChanges schema description -- which was ALSO stale, listing only 3 of the 7 tracked fields. The documented escape hatch is free and was live-proven: a label's first run on a wider filter set is a 0-charge baseline, so seeding with all 4 statuses recorded all 2033 wildfire opportunities (closed+archived included) at 0 charged. Verified on 0.1.37: blind run -> 2 untruncated warnings + both filters listed; all-4-statuses run -> [] and no warning; default-input gate 10/10 charged, no regression; all 8 standing checks clean; 3 test KV baselines deleted.
